# Removing or downgrading x requires upgrading a. The old x requires a
# higher b too, but once a is upgraded, nothing needs that version of b.
cp go.mod go.mod.orig
go get example.com/x@none
go list -m -f '{{.Path}} {{.Version}}' all
stdout '^example.com/a v1.1.0$'
stdout '^example.com/b v1.0.0$'
! stdout '^example.com/x '

cp go.mod.orig go.mod
go get example.com/x@v0.9.0
go list -m -f '{{.Path}} {{.Version}}' all
stdout '^example.com/a v1.1.0$'
stdout '^example.com/b v1.0.0$'
stdout '^example.com/x v0.9.0$'

# If the new a still requires the higher b, retain that upgrade.
cp go.mod.orig go.mod
cp a1/go.mod.with-b a1/go.mod
go get example.com/x@none
go list -m -f '{{.Path}} {{.Version}}' all
stdout '^example.com/a v1.1.0$'
stdout '^example.com/b v1.5.0$'
! stdout '^example.com/x '

-- go.mod --
module example.com/app

go 1.23

require (
	example.com/a v1.0.0
	example.com/b v1.0.0
)

replace (
	example.com/a v1.0.0 => ./a0
	example.com/a v1.1.0 => ./a1
	example.com/b => ./b
	example.com/x v0.9.0 => ./x0
	example.com/x v1.0.0 => ./x1
)
-- app.go --
package app

import (
	_ "example.com/a"
	_ "example.com/b"
)
-- a0/go.mod --
module example.com/a

go 1.23

require example.com/x v1.0.0
-- a0/a.go --
package a
-- a1/go.mod --
module example.com/a

go 1.23
-- a1/go.mod.with-b --
module example.com/a

go 1.23

require example.com/b v1.5.0
-- a1/a.go --
package a
-- b/go.mod --
module example.com/b

go 1.23
-- b/b.go --
package b
-- x0/go.mod --
module example.com/x

go 1.23
-- x0/x.go --
package x
-- x1/go.mod --
module example.com/x

go 1.23

require (
	example.com/a v1.1.0
	example.com/b v1.5.0
)
-- x1/x.go --
package x
